citations.narrative:
At the time of inspection, two sheltered kennels were found with the temperature of the interior sheltered portion above 85
degrees Fahrenheit. Using the inspector’s kestrel, the temperature in the “aussie building” was measured at 97 degrees,
and the puppy building was measured at 94 degrees F at approximately 1pm in the afternoon. Additional ventilation was
started in both kennels and the temperature was rechecked at approximately 2:45pm. The temperature in the “aussie
building” was at 94 degrees F and the puppy building was at 97.1 degrees F. Two new window air conditioning units were
obtained and installed in the buildings after the second temperature check. The temperature in the “aussie building” was
rechecked a third time at 5:30pm and was found to be between 91.1 and 93.1 degrees F in different areas of the building.
The puppy building was rechecked at approximately 5:35 and found to be at 94.2 degrees F. According to weather
archives, the outdoor temperature in the area was recorded being between 97 and 99 degrees Fahrenheit from 1pm to
5pm and an extreme heat advisory was in place.
At the initial inspection, the dogs in the kennel did not appear to be in distress and many were observed playing in their
enclosures. At the time of the 5:30pm rechecks, multiple puppies were observed panting heavily with several appearing
lethargic, laying on their side, and/or breathing heavily. In the “aussie building” there was a newborn litter of six poodle
puppies with their dam. Puppies that young are unable to effectively regulate their body temperature and can become
heat stressed easily. In total, there were eighteen puppies ranging from newborn to 8 weeks of age and nine adults in the
“aussie building” and eleven puppies in the puppy building.
Exposure to temperature extremes can result in discomfort, stress, illness, and death in animals.
The sheltered portion of sheltered housing facilities for dogs and cats must be sufficiently heated and cooled when
necessary to protect the health and well-being of the animals. The licensee must ensure that ambient temperature does
not fall below 45 degrees F or rise above 85 degrees F for more than four consecutive hours when dogs and cats are
present.
To be corrected: September 8, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
Additional Inspectors:
ERIKA LEISNER, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
